utterances.text: And it refers to the former SFRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And that would indicate that at least the Canadian Government thought that the SFRY had ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us look at the letter D/18/3, the letter dated May 6th from the Canadian Ambassador to the United Nations. That would seem to indicate that the Canadian Government had recognised the creation of the FRY, and had serious questions about the FRY's right as a sole successor to the Socialist Federal Republic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With care for the word, "recognition", I think it acknowledges the declaration of the FRY and the subsequent information about that declaration to the United Nations and raises the question about...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And would seem to indicate that everybody is agreed that the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that the Canadian Ambassador and the Canadian Government thinks that the SFRY had ceased to exist as of 6 May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure that it absolutely indicates that, but it is certainly consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: It is consistent with that kind of belief. D/19/3 is a letter from the Deputy Representative of the United States. Again, it talks about serious questions of whether the FRY is a continuation of the SFRY. That would lead one to believe that the policy of the United States was that the Socialist Federal Republic had ceased to exist as of 5 May. Would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that is the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And D/16/3 is a note by the President of the Security Council, and it refers to the release of a numbered United Nations document, the number being S/23877?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which is the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Which is the declaration from the FRY government of its creation. That would seem to indicate that there was at least some question within the Security Council about the right of the FRY to be a successor state? It is very carefully worded, but you would agree with me that it is an indication of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an indication that there is taken to be a new political fact and that fact is being acknowledged without prejudice to any other questions, including succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And it would lead one to believe that there was general agreement at least within the Security Council that the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had ceased to exist, and that there was a new entity out there called the FRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think there was generally de facto political recognition that the SFRY, well, if not had ceased to exist was not going to continue for some time and that I think there is a general acceptance that on the political, on a political level, the declaration of the formation of the FRY is -- that the event which formally ends the SFRY's existence, and that is the point at which the process of dissolution is terminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But a number of questions continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sure. On April 27th the SFRY --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If no earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: But clearly, by that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, if you are done with that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I am done with those documents, your Honour, and it would be a convenient place to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have one matter to ask the court about. Mr. Landzo would like to be excused from the courtroom on Monday and Tuesday, February 16th and 17th. The Red Cross has graciously provided for a visit from his family from Bosnia and they will be here Monday and Tuesday, and he would like to have that time off to be able to visit with his family at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose it is with consultation with you as counsel, it should be sufficient. We do not really need him for such an exercise on Monday and Tuesday. So, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I thank you for letting me continue a little bit long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are now adjourned until Monday. (5.45 pm)
